title: Interview Evidence Workpad + Role Decision Simulator
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, interviewer-friendly workpad to capture evidence during loops and to run a short decision 'simulator' at offer time. Goal: reduce bias, speed consensus, and produce an actionable first-30-day onboarding sketch from the same notes. Meant for mid-senior IC and manager roles across eng/product/infra.

How to use (quick):
- Interviewers: fill the Evidence rows live (concise bullets, 1-2 lines each). Mark confidence (low/med/high).
- Hiring manager + recruiter: run the Decision Simulator after collecting all evidence. Follow the numeric thresholds but use override comments when needed.
- People Ops: use the resulting onboarding sketch to pre-fill role kickoff and first-week calendar.

1) Candidate snapshot (one-line):
- Name: __________________  Role: __________________  Cycle stage: onsite / final loop
- Recruiter score (0-10): __  Hiring mgr initial lean (for/neutral/against): __

2) Evidence capture template (for each interviewer) — keep terse:
- Competency (pick 1): system-design | coding | infra | product-sense | leadership | execution
- Top 2 evidence bullets (concrete):
  * Bullet 1 - what they said/did (quote or paraphrase)
  * Bullet 2 - consequence/impact or tradeoffs they considered
- Red flags (if any): __
- Strengths summary (1 line): __
- Confidence: low / med / high

3) Scoring grid (per interviewer) — numeric quick-scan:
- Competency score (1-5): __
- Culture / collaboration (1-5): __
- Communication clarity (1-5): __
- Autonomy & ownership signal (1-5): __
- Net = sum (4-20)
- Notes on calibration vs role bar (anchor: role bar = 14 for senior IC, 16 for staff, 18+ for principal)

4) Decision Simulator (hiring mgr + recruiter run together)
Steps:
  A) Collect all interviewer Nets and average -> AvgNet (round down).
  B) Compute confidence multiplier: if >60% interviewers marked "high" confidence then +1 bonus to AvgNet.
  C) Apply red-flag veto: any interviewer with >1 documented red flag triggers a red-flag review. If unresolved, auto-defer.
  D) Offer rule (default):
     - If AvgNet + bonus >= role bar => recommend OFFER.
     - If AvgNet within (role bar -2) and at least 2 interviewers called "strengths" = go-to-hire but needs hiring manager rationale (include leveling justification).
     - If AvgNet < (role bar -2) => NO OFFER / consider other role.
  E) Tie-breaker: hiring manager qualitative endorsement can override +1 point but must be documented with specific risk mitigations.

5) Offer packet checklist (if decision = OFFER)
- Target level & comp band checked with recruiting comp guide (attach comp doc link)
- Baseline relocation/remote terms clarified
- Proposed start date within 3 weeks? yes/no
- Interviewer praise snippets (pick 2 lines for offer mail)
- Onboarding sketch attached (first 30 days, see below)

6) First-30-day onboarding sketch (auto-draft fields; people ops + hiring mgr edit)
Week 0 (before start): device & access checklist assigned; buddy assigned; pre-reads (arch overview, team OKRs)
Week 1: orientation, intro meetings w/ direct partners, small focused task w/ clear acceptance criteria (deliverable: PR or doc)
Weeks 2-4: ramp plan with 3 micro-goals (1 cross-team integration, 1 code/infra task, 1 product/impact deliverable); weekly sync cadence; feedback checkpoints at day 14 and day 30.
Risk mitigations (if skill gaps flagged): dedicated mentoring slot twice-weekly for first 4 weeks; pair-programming sessions; stretch timeline for autonomy from week 6 -> 8.

7) Interviewer calibration notes (short):
- Use evidence-first language. Avoid hypothetical praise. Anchor to examples: "led X, reduced Y by Z%".
- If you are unsure about level, mark "level unsure" not just high/low. Provide 2 signals that would move you toward staff/principal.

8) Candidate-care + communication schedule (recruiter checklist):
- Day after onsite: send thank-you + TLDR next steps (template snippet below)
- 3 business days: follow-up with timeline or decision
- If offer: keep candidate live with hiring mgr intro note and first-week sketch
- If no-offer: provide 1-2 pieces of actionable feedback (no longer than 3 bullets) and invite to future loops where fit might change

9) Example filled mini-case (for clarity):
- AvgNet = 15, confidence bonus +1 => 16, role bar=16 -> OFFER recommended. Hiring mgr provides leveling rationale (candidate has 3 yrs infra ownership + delivered multi-region migration).

10) Unresolved questions (tracker) — things to close before final decision:
- unclear: candidate's scope owning cross-team dependencies? (owner: Hiring mgr)
- unclear: compensation alignment for relocation? (owner: recruiter)
- docs to pull: previous performance repo links or public work samples (owner: interviewer)

11) Quick templates / snippets (copy-paste)
- Post-onsite thank you (short): "Thanks again for meeting with the team — we appreciated the systems thinking you showed on X. We’ll close loop by EOD Friday with next steps."
- Offer praise lines (pick two): "Showed clear ownership of end-to-end delivery" / "Deep tradeoff awareness on latency vs cost" / "Strong mentorship instinct with concrete examples"

12) Next steps for people-ops (meta):
- Run a quarterly calibration workshop where we sample 15 hires and compare evidence -> leveling decisions.
- Maintain a short bank (internal) of 6 exemplar evidence snippets per role family (to speed interviewer calibration).

Notes / meta: this doc is intentionally compact — use as the canonical capture artifact for loops that need fast closure. We're testing the numeric thresholds for 6 weeks (A/B across two hiring cohorts). Feedback to Priya Nair (people-ops) or drop notes in #people-hiring channel.
